hints: Focus on the shape of each molecule, because only flat shapes like linear, bent with 3 atoms, trigonal planar allow all atoms to sit in one plane.
Remember that pyramidal molecules like $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{PH}_3$ are not flat, so any set containing them can be ruled out straight away.
Check the tricky $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ carefully, its methyl group is tetrahedral so not all its atoms can be planar, leaving only one set where ethene, carbon dioxide and water are all flat.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a molecule planar**

Think about shape from VSEPR theory. Linear molecules and any molecule with only 3 atoms are always flat, because 2 or 3 points always define a plane. Trigonal planar is also flat, but pyramidal and tetrahedral are not.

Rule to use:
$$\text{planar shapes} = \text{linear, bent (3 atoms), trigonal planar}$$

**Sort the small molecules**

$\text{BF}_3$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$ (as single molecules) are trigonal planar with 3 bond pairs and no lone pairs, so they are planar. $\text{CO}_2$ is linear $\text{O=C=O}$, so planar. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is bent but has only 3 atoms, so those 3 atoms must lie in one plane.

$$\text{planar: } \text{BF}_3, \text{AlCl}_3, \text{CO}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Spot the non-planar molecules**

$\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{PH}_3$ are both trigonal pyramidal with 3 bond pairs plus 1 lone pair, just like ammonia. The central atom sits above the base, so they are 3D, not flat. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (ethene) is flat around the $\text{C=C}$, but $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ as propene contains a $\text{CH}_3$ group which is tetrahedral, so its H atoms stick out of the plane.

$$\text{non-planar: } \text{NH}_3, \text{PH}_3, \text{C}_3\text{H}_6$$

**Choose the all-planar set**

Only the set with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has three planar members with no pyramidal or tetrahedral parts. That is the answer.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{BF}_3$ are both trigonal planar and flat, but $\text{PH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal like $\text{NH}_3$. Its lone pair pushes the P above the three H atoms, so not all atoms are in one plane.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{AlCl}_3$ is planar and $\text{CO}_2$ is linear and planar, but $\text{NH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal with a lone pair. It is 3-dimensional, so this set fails the test.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{BF}_3$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ are both planar, which is tempting, but $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ spoils it. As propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$, the $\text{CH}_3$ carbon is tetrahedral, and as cyclopropane the H atoms lie above and below the ring, so all atoms cannot be in one plane.
options.D: Correct. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is planar with trigonal planar carbons around the double bond, $\text{CO}_2$ is linear $\text{O=C=O}$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is bent but with only 3 atoms they must define a single plane. Well done, all three are flat.
